apps.changeLog:
### New

- **Snippets:** save a message, a piece of selected text or your draft as a snippet from its menu or the `#` picker. In Settings you can rename a snippet, move it between project and global, and preview what it expands to.
- **Images:** agents can generate images with an image model you pick in Settings > General > OpenChamber Tools. The pictures show in the chat with a download button. Off by default.
- **Auto-review:** the review loop keeps going when you close the tab or lock the phone. It stops after five rounds, notifies you once when it ends, and a disputed result shows both positions in place.
- Header tabs: a new option keeps separate tabs for each project and worktree, and shows the tabs of the place you are in.
- Agents: an agent can wait on its pull request and wakes up when a check fails or passes, someone comments, or it is merged. The composer shows the pull request with Stop watching.
- Sidebar: pin a worktree from its menu to keep it on top. "Name worktrees by branch" in the display menu shows the branch first.
- Terminal: a tab closes when its shell or action exits. Turn it off in Settings > General > Terminal to keep the output.
- Drafts: a new session shows "N drafts" when other drafts wait in the same folder, to open or discard them.
- Dictation: Whisper large-v3 turbo and Qwen3-ASR join the local models, the dictation language helps them recognize short phrases, and "Fix misheard words" can clean up the text with the Small Model.
- Appearance: Interface font weight under Density & type, from Regular to Strong.
- Usage: the OpenCode Go page shows your OpenCode Console budgets.
- The app tells a small joke now and then: in the new-session heading, on a clean Git panel, after a late-night push. Pushes and merges throw confetti.

### Improvements

- Sidebar: each row shows what it is on the left and its state on the right, project headers read as sections, and times and branches are easier to read. A worktree is named by its task, never by one of its sessions.
- Sidebar: Track and Done sit only on rows that are a work of their own, and a fork is a work of its own.
- New session: the first message shows at once while the session is created, and a second Enter cannot start a second session (thanks to @yulia-ivashko).
- Work Status: the card stays beside Files, Changes or the browser when the window has room for both.
- Themes: secondary text, links and quotes are readable in every built-in theme, and dark themes keep secondary text quieter than the body.
- Files: document toolbars share one look and keep their buttons in place, and Files can comment on a whole file from its toolbar.
- Files: an open file or plan updates as soon as it changes on disk.
- Composer: `@` session search keeps matching across the words of a title.
- Small Model: a session on a small model such as DeepSeek or GLM flash keeps side work on that model.
- Worktrees: an issue worktree keeps the agent's branch name with the issue number in front, such as `fix/5747-stale-favorite-models`.

### Fixes

- Providers: connecting with an API key or OAuth works on the first try.
- Sessions: while a session runs in a folder with many sessions, the app no longer sends about a gigabyte an hour to OpenCode.
- Git: GitHub Enterprise and self-hosted GitLab behind a company certificate connect.
- Windows: upgrading OpenCode from the app no longer leaves OpenCode broken until a reinstall.
- Worktrees: deleting a worktree that sits on main no longer offers to delete main (thanks to @yulia-ivashko).
- Sessions: a session moved to another folder leaves no copy behind (thanks to @yulia-ivashko), and permission cards reach a session the agent moved mid-turn (thanks to @mossgowild).
- Sidebar: sessions in work outside your projects stay in In work (thanks to @alohaninja).
- Sidebar: a click anywhere on a row opens it, and a dragged session lands only in the folder under the pointer.
- Issues and PRs: a folder with several GitHub checkouts shows the list instead of a validation error (thanks to @guidan-nick).
- Desktop: a notification for another instance opens in the window that shows it (thanks to @timothywang21).
- Desktop: the update download progress stops at 100% (thanks to @bashrusakh).
- Desktop: the dock badge counts only chats the sidebar shows.
- Browser: an app in the agent's hidden tab runs at full speed.
- Settings/Providers: a custom provider kept in `opencode.jsonc` can be edited (thanks to @yulia-ivashko).
- Skills: turning a skill off works in projects with non-Latin folder names (thanks to @yulia-ivashko).
- Plugins: enable and disable rules in the plugin list no longer show as broken plugins.
- Chat: a link to a folder opens it in Finder (thanks to @yulia-ivashko).
- Chat: reference chips no longer cut off letters.
- Models: the favorite-model shortcut skips favorites whose provider is disconnected.
- Header: the session menu offers Move to project when session tabs are off.
- Composer: the cross in the drafts menu discards the draft instead of opening it.
- Comments: the whole-file comment field opens where you are in a long file.
- Folder trust: the app asks again when a local file a trusted plugin imports changes.
- Web: a page whose first load failed retries instead of staying empty.
- CLI: `openchamber serve` started from the app's terminal serves its own build.

### Misc

- Bundled OpenCode updated to 2.2.0, now the minimum supported version.
- Git library updated past four published security advisories.
- Desktop: Help > Suggest a Feature opens a feature request.

Notify FileExplorerFragment via LocalBroadcast when ephemeral worker tasks
(upload, delete, move) finish, ensuring the file list refreshes automatically
and cached entries are invalidated.

* Disable Icon Tint For Thumbnails
The introduction of themes seemed to apply tint globally to multiple View elements, including the ImageView used to display thumbnails. Consequently, while Glide would successfully load thumbnails, they would render as completely white or black (depending on the theme). We can workaround this by dynamically disabling tint when using Glide to load thumbnails.

This fixes https://github.com/newhinton/Round-Sync/issues/166 and https://github.com/newhinton/Round-Sync/issues/310 .

Credit: Proposed by @viche12345 in https://github.com/newhinton/Round-Sync/pull/332

apps.changeLog:
# 🚀 What's Changed
Hey! **v2.0.0 is now ready** 👀. I have been working on this update for over 2 months, which is why there was no new release and non-major bugs did not get patched.

This release includes a few bug fixes, but the main change is a **FULL REFACTORING** (#1) of the audio capture logic. **The scrcpy-server binary is gone**. We now **handle audio capture natively** with code in our own app. This gives us direct control over PCM audio which this release already makes some use of, and may in the future make even more.

I also want to announce that **we now support VoIP / IN_COMMUNICATION type of audio capture starting Android 14**. (So **most third-party apps and carriers using VoIP or Wi-Fi Calling**!). I know I said at multiple places online that it would be starting Android 13, but hum, how do I say this.. Oops, the shell has one permission missing in that version that SPECIFICALLY prevents IN_COMMUNICATION capture and I tested everything except specifically capturing that... 😅

That said, I still want to credit the scrcpy project as I would not have been able to do it without using their code as reference. While I inspired myself and had to make adjustments along with implementing more methods, they still laid out the base work that allowed me to know how it worked and where in AOSP source code I needed to look.

I also want to thank everyone who decided to sponsor me via [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/kitsumed). ❤️ I'm still amazed I even managed to get 4 monthly sponsors, let alone occasional one-time sponsors.

I will remind you again, but if you use this project often, please consider supporting me. If you do not wish to do it via money, you can still contribute. For example, **this new v2.0.0 release is missing translations**. You can help on [Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/shizucallrecorder/).

Last minute edit: While updating packages, I was forced to support Android 17. So, **Android 17 R1 release is now supported**, updated some reflection stuff. That said, if your Shizuku versions does not work with Android 17, then report the issue to your Shizuku repository, not me.

## 🔭 The future of this project
**v2.0.0 is what I wanted v1.x.x to be.** A native call recording application. This was my original goal when I first started the project, but at the time, I did not know Android development well, never used Kotlin, Android Studio, read parts of AOSP source code, nor did I know about reflection. My solution was to use the scrcpy-server binary, and little by little, I started learning more and I somehow pulled it off over the last 2 months.

In that regard, I partially see ShizuCallRecorder current position as feature complete / *partially* in a bug-fix lifecycle. The app is working well for almost all users. **There are still more features I wish to add.** For example, https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/3, which would also cause a rework of how the UI works. Then, that UI rework may cause another plan of mine, https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/97 (adding support to connect to ADB ourselves without Shizuku).

I have increasingly wanted to do this because I am not satisfied with the practices of most "updated/popular" Shizuku forks. Their unsafe security and release practices, along with heavy AI/LLM agent usage without a lot of human interaction. We can also add to that their tendencies of mixing tons of other forks features into their own using an LLM, which makes questionable implementations and default configurations.

I am also interested in this because it would allow me to enforce a safer way of making the app work and give me direct control over more failure points. It does, however, worry me, as Shizuku in itself is a complex app, mainly due to the complexity of supporting different manufacturers (OEMs).

For the time being, I continue to recommend thedjchi Shizuku fork, as they offered good security options inside the app, were very open and receptive to security-related requests, and ensured their release CI/process was using the best security they could once notified about it. Sadly, they are currently no longer maintaining the fork, but it is still working as of writing this. I have yet to find another fork which makes me feel comfortable using it, let alone recommend it.

The next new feature you *may* soon see is a new call detection method based on notifications (https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/131), because while we can now start recording third-party apps on Android 14+, not all apps use Android Telecom, which is currently the only way we can detect calls. Notification-based detection could be a workaround for a low number of users / weird apps. Please note, however, that I do not wish to implement advanced support for all kinds of third-party apps, I want my support to be best-effort focused and as generic as possible to prevent maintenance burdens as soon as an X third-party app makes an update.

Last minute edit: **If you have some free time, I recommend checking out [Android May Soon Restrict On-Device ADB](https://kitsumed.github.io/blog/posts/android-may-soon-restrict-on-device-adb/)** as this may affect the future of this project. Hopefully it won't.

## More Details On Changes
* refractor: **Native audio handling**. The *big big* **audio rework** by @kitsumed in https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/pull/132
* Fixed a bug causing unexpected folder creation when contact name contains forward slash (/) and was used in the file name template. (https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/125)
* **VoIP / third-party apps recording is now possible starting Android 14+** on non-pixel devices (https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/13 , https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/130)
* **New audio codecs**, xHE-AAC, HE-AAC v2, AMR WB and more along with **more bitrate options**! (https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/49)
* **You can now split uplink and downlink audio on separate channel (left/right)** of the recording. (https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/73)
* Fixed a regression that in specific scenario caused the app to add `+` to a short phone number. (https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/issues/114)
* **Android 17 Support** (R1 release, did not test) and bumped packages along with phone number metadata https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/commit/23a7b7b0df2433012f04600c706135064cfb07ee
* Updated Gradle to 9.8.2 https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/commit/8f4095c436942f5fb59a7b7468b7485a2dfc6fd6
* Bumped GitHub Actions versions and switched to pinned commit https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/commit/b0f63a614a40344bcca02668533ce398fcdb7d2c
* Updated translations


## Contributors
* Translations : @oersen @camellan @avishj @Guzleon @kitsumed @Mehrshad0101 and everyone else who have been missed or did not link their github account to weblate.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/kitsumed/ShizuCallRecorder/compare/v1.3.3...v2.0.0
**This is a tool, use it responsibly, and follow the law. Read the app disclaimer, it's a one time thing, don't skip it.**
